---
title: "The agent context & collaboration system"
subtitle: "One principal per project, workers on demand, files as the memory"
toc: true
number-sections: true
---

Flux treats an AI agent as a first-class user: everything the app can do, an agent can do
through files and typed verbs. On top of that sits a **standing collaborator per project —
the principal** — which knows who you are and what the project is trying to achieve,
takes your feedback without you leaving the app, and **dispatches worker agents** for
substantial analysis and coding.

Two principles carry the whole design:

1. **The files are the memory.** Everything the system knows lives in two plain-text
   `Context` folders. Any agent CLI can be the principal or a worker; swapping vendors
   or models is a launch-time choice, and continuity comes from *rehydration* — the
   principal writes its memory down as it works, so a fresh session picks up exactly
   where the last one stopped.
2. **Your terminal is the cockpit.** Sessions run in *your* terminals (as many as you
   like, across projects); the Flux app is the review surface — figures, manuscripts,
   comments, feedback — and works independently alongside them.

# Talking to the principal

From a terminal in (or near) a Flux project:

```bash
flux principal
```

A minimal picker appears — **Principal** and **Workers** rows, each *family · model ·
effort*, pre-filled with your last choice — so a bare **Enter launches immediately**
(`p`/`w` customize a row, `q` quits). The session then runs right there, in whatever
terminal stack you use (ghostty, zellij, tmux, ssh — all fine), with three things done
for you:

- **Boot**: the agent receives the machine-resolved boot prompt and reads its way in —
  your `UserContext`, the stock doctrine, the project's mission/notebook/rules, the
  journal tail, open feedback — then opens with a **standup**. On a fresh project it
  *interviews you* and drafts the mission instead.
- **Transcripts**: the rendered conversation is captured to `Context/Transcripts/`
  (a PTY interposer + headless terminal — works identically under any terminal;
  `--no-transcript` opts out).
- **Environment**: `FLUX_PROJECT`, identity, the worker policy, and MCP wiring are set
  so the typed Flux tools (inline figure PNGs, the live bridge) point at the right
  project.

Run as many principals as you have projects — one per zellij pane if you like. The
sessions are independent; each project's Context keeps its own memory.

**Resuming:** prefer a fresh `flux principal` — rehydration reads *current* files, while
a resumed conversation remembers stale ones. For genuinely mid-thought work, the vendor's
own resume works (e.g. `codex resume <id>` — the id is printed at session end and
captured in the transcript); run it from the project directory so MCP roots correctly.

# Workers

The principal dispatches workers itself:

```bash
flux dispatch <name> --brief-file brief.md [--model m --effort e]
```

Under the default **"principal decides"** policy, the principal picks each worker's
model and effort per task (its boot prompt carries the menu and guidance: mechanical
work low/medium, hard analysis high tiers); a fixed policy from the picker applies
automatically. Every dispatch is recorded in `Context/Dispatches/<stamp>-<name>/` —
`brief.md` (the exact instructions), `log.txt` (live-streaming output; `tail -f` it to
watch a worker think), and `result.md` (outcome + the agent used). The principal reviews
each result against the mission before you see it.

# Where everything lives

Run `flux config` for this machine's resolved paths.

**Machine level — `<FluxConfig>/`:**

| Path | What | Who writes |
|---|---|---|
| `Context/UserContext/` | `WHO-AM-I.md` (you) + `RULES.md` (your standing rules) + any files you add | **You** |
| `Context/FluxContext/` | The stock docs — the single canonical home of agent-facing Flux knowledge (doctrine, workflow, every verb, slides, python/uv conventions, Lighttable…). Re-synced on every Flux update with machine paths baked in. | **Flux** |
| `agents.json` | The roster **matrix**: per-vendor command templates + their model/effort menus, and standing defaults (see @sec-roster) | **You** |

**Project level — `<project>/Context/`** (scaffolded for new projects; healed into old
ones on first open, or via `flux context-init`):

| Path | What | Who writes |
|---|---|---|
| `Project/MISSION.qmd` | The charter: question, data, deliverable, scope | Co-owned — you have final say |
| `NOTEBOOK.md` | The principal's memory: state, decisions + why, dead ends, session log | **The agent** — you read + comment |
| `RULES.md` | Project rules; recurring feedback gets promoted here | Co-owned |
| `Transcripts/` | Session transcripts (machine-captured) | **Flux** |
| `Dispatches/` | Worker briefs/logs/results | **The principal** |

Mission, notebook, and rules are **first-class Flux Paper documents** — they appear in
the document picker's Context group, and **margin comments work on them**: annotate your
agent's understanding or memory and it treats those threads as corrections. The
operational machinery (`.meta/feedback.ndjson` ledger, `journal.ndjson` provenance,
attend state) lives in `.meta/` and takes care of itself.

# The review loop (in the app)

- **Comments** on any document — threaded, anchored to exact text.
- **Ctrl+Shift+M** anywhere — "Note to agent": one line, automatically **stamped with
  what you're looking at** (figure/element/plot part, document + selected text, slide +
  beat). **Send** marks the boundary: everything open becomes the work order.
- The principal drains both queues (`flux feedback`, `flux comments`), fixes each item,
  and resolves it with a note — threads close live in your margin. When unsure, it asks
  *you* via a margin comment instead of guessing.
- **While you're away**: leave `flux attend` running — your Send wakes one
  non-interactive principal pass that drains the queue and updates the notebook.
- **In the reader**: ✦ Ask AI opens the shared in-app terminal pane and *prefills* a
  question about your selection or highlight (run `flux principal` in that pane — or
  anywhere; any session can read the live reader state via `get_reading_context`). The
  same shared terminal is available in the Paper margin.
- **⌘K palette**: open mission/notebook/rules, global rules, Note to agent, and *Copy
  principal prompt* (paste the boot prompt into any existing session).

# The roster — `agents.json` {#sec-roster}

The full reference is `FluxContext/AGENTS-CONFIG.md`. Shape:

``` json
{
  "families": {
    "codex":  { "models": ["gpt-5.6-sol", "gpt-5.6-terra", "gpt-5.6-luna"],
                "efforts": ["low", "medium", "high", "xhigh"],
                "interactive": ["codex", "--model", "{model}", "…", "{prompt}"],
                "exec":        ["codex", "exec", "--model", "{model}", "…", "{prompt}"] },
    "claude": { "models": ["fable", "opus", "sonnet"], "efforts": ["default"], "…": "…" }
  },
  "defaults": {
    "principal": { "family": "codex", "model": "gpt-5.6-sol", "effort": "xhigh" },
    "worker":    { "family": "codex", "model": "principal-decides", "effort": "principal-decides" },
    "pass":      { "family": "codex", "model": "gpt-5.6-sol", "effort": "xhigh" }
  }
}
```

Families are command *templates* (`{model}`/`{effort}` substitute inside args; `{prompt}`,
`{mcpJson}`, etc. resolve at launch); the picker menus come from each family's lists.
**This file is the whole vendor coupling** — pick a different family and your
collaborator gets a new brain with the same memory.

# Design properties

- **Agent-agnostic by construction**: plain files, spawned CLIs, terminal-host
  transcripts — no vendor session stores, formats, or UI surfaces to chase.
- **Crash-safe**: the ledger is append-only; attend state survives restarts; a dead
  session loses nothing that was written down.
- **Auditable**: briefs, worker logs, transcripts, the journal, and the notebook record
  what every agent did and why — including which model/effort ran each task.
- **Self-improving**: feedback that expresses a preference gets promoted into RULES;
  decisions land in the notebook as they're made. Session ten needs less correcting
  than session one.

# Troubleshooting

- `flux: command not found` → `~/.local/bin` missing or off PATH (the shim installs
  there on first run); the full path always works — see `docs/installation.qmd`.
- A verb says `deferred: … is locked` → you're mid-edit in the app; the agent retries.
  That's the coexistence model working.
- Old project without `Context/` → open it once in the app, or `flux context-init`.
- The picker shows a "legacy roster" note → your `agents.json` uses the old
  fixed-command form; it still works, or reseed with the matrix schema.
